reason: E1 demonstrates that O/N interstitials cause phase segregation and softening in a TiVNbTa refractory HEA at 700°C, supporting the first two premises. However, E1 does not study a Ti–Ni-based HEA, nor does it test an ultra-high purity processing route or mechanical properties above 700°C; the extrapolation to a different alloy system and the claimed benefit of the intervention are therefore unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Trace oxygen/nitrogen interstitials promote phase segregation during high-temperature exposure in refractory HEAs
Interstitial-driven phase segregation depletes the matrix of strengthening solutes, causing softening
Reducing impurity uptake during processing will suppress this segregation and softening
The Ti–Ni HEA will behave similarly to the TiVNbTa alloy studied in E1
